**Dark-mode primary: `#7bacfc`**

I checked it with `klar contrast #7bacfc #1a1a2e` and got an OKCA contrast of 4.5 on `#1a1a2e`. That meets your body-text AA threshold exactly, with no margin.

The brand `#3b82f6` only reaches 1.9 on that surface. Lightening alone can't get it to 4.5. `klar find` topped out at 2.2 (`#438aff`) and exited 1, meaning the target was unreachable. Getting to 4.5 needed some desaturation as well.

| | OKLCH | Contrast on #1a1a2e |
|---|---|---|
| Brand `#3b82f6` | L 0.648, C 0.188, H 259.8 | 1.9 |
| Dark mode `#7bacfc` | L 0.743, C 0.128, H 259.8 | 4.5 |

- **Hue:** unchanged at 259.8°, so it still reads as the same blue.
- **Distance from the brand color:** ΔE is 13. Lightness rose by about 0.10 and chroma dropped by about 0.06. The result is a lighter, softer blue.
- **Method:** I used `klar find --allow-desaturation`, which returns the closest color that reaches the target.
- **Margin:** if you want headroom against rounding or rendering differences, run `klar find` with `--target 4.6` or `4.7`. The color will move a little further from the brand blue.

0.75 at chroma 0.13 is out of gamut, so I'm lowering the top chroma step to 0.115.

Here is the 4×3 grid, all at hue 259.81° (the hue of #3b82f6). Contrast is OKCA with the shade as foreground on #ffffff, and AA body text needs 4.5 or more. I measured each cell with `klar contrast <hex> "#fff" --json`.

| OKLCH L ↓ / C → | C 0.04 (muted) | C 0.08 (medium) | C 0.115 (vivid) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0.75** | `#9fafc8` 1.7 ❌ | `#90afe1` 1.7 ❌ | `#82aff7` 1.7 ❌ |
| **0.623** | `#7988a0` 2.9 ❌ | `#6a88b8` 2.9 ❌ | `#5d87cc` 2.9 ❌ |
| **0.50** | `#56647a` 5.0 ✅ | `#486491` 5.0 ✅ | `#3a62a4` 5.0 ✅ |
| **0.38** | `#364358` 8.8 ✅ | `#28426d` 8.8 ✅ | `#19407e` 8.8 ✅ |

- **Pass for body text on white:** the bottom two rows (L 0.50 and 0.38), all six shades.
- **Fail:** the top two rows. The L 0.623 row is the same lightness as #3b82f6 itself, which scores 2.9 on white.
- **Contrast follows lightness, not chroma.** Each row has the same score across all three chroma steps, so lightness is the only lever for passing. If you want a brand-blue text color, L 0.50 is the lightest step that passes.
- **Chroma steps are lower than #3b82f6's own (0.188).** At L 0.75 and 0.38, chroma above about 0.12 falls outside sRGB. I used 0.04, 0.08 and 0.115 so every cell is a real in-gamut color and the whole grid is comparable.
- **Why I didn't use `klar variants`.** With `--light-steps 4 --chroma-steps 3`, 6 of the 12 cells come back empty because they are out of gamut. The adaptive default sizes the grid on its own and doesn't give a fixed 4×3.

I built the grid with a small OKLCH-to-hex script in `/tmp/o.py` and did not write anything into the project.

The closest passing color is **`#7bacfc`**, but it costs saturation, so it needs a brand sign-off from you. It's a visible shift: ΔE 13 from `#3b82f6`.

**Measurements** (OKCA, foreground on background, `#1a1a2e`):

| Color | OKCA | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `#3b82f6` (brand) | 1.9 | fails 4.5 |
| Best lightness-only shift (`#438aff`) | 2.2 | fails 4.5 |
| **`#7bacfc`** | **4.5** | passes AA body text |

**Why lightness alone can't fix it.** At the brand's chroma (0.188) and hue (260°), the blue can only be displayed within a narrow lightness band, roughly L 0.47 to 0.65. Nothing lighter exists in sRGB at that saturation. The lightness-only search topped out at 2.2, so klar reported the target as unreachable.

**What the fix changes.** `#7bacfc` keeps the hue exactly (259.8°). Lightness rises from 0.62 to 0.74, and chroma drops from 0.188 to 0.128, so it reads as a lighter, softer blue. It sits exactly on 4.5, so it has no headroom.

**Options:**
- **Adopt `#7bacfc`** as the dark-mode primary text color. This is the closest option that passes.
- **Keep `#3b82f6` for non-text uses on dark**, such as icons, borders and large text. It fails those thresholds on this surface too (1.9 against 3.0), so it would need a separate check.
- **Use a lighter tint than `#7bacfc`.** This buys headroom above 4.5, at the cost of a bigger shift from the brand blue.

Two pairs are degenerate: `text` on `surface-dark` and `inverse` on `surface` are the same color, so they score 1.0. I assume you never place them that way, so I excluded them from the failure count. If those combinations are possible, tell me and I'll treat them as failures.

## Proposed fixes

The background stays fixed and I adjust the foreground. "ΔE" is klar's reported color shift, in OKLCH-based ΔE units. A single token can't serve both backgrounds, so the primary, accent and success fixes are theme-specific variants.

| Pair | Current | Proposed | New contrast | ΔE | How it changes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| primary on surface | #3b82f6 | **#115bcc** | 5.0 | 15 | Darker; hue and chroma kept |
| accent on surface | #e94560 | **#bf103f** | 4.7 | 13 | Darker; hue and chroma kept |
| success on surface | #22c55e | **#047f38** | 4.6 | 22 | Darker and desaturated (C 0.192→0.144) |
| primary on surface-dark | #3b82f6 | **#7bacfc** | 4.5 | 13 | Lighter and desaturated (C 0.188→0.128) |
| accent on surface-dark | #e94560 | **#fe8a93** | 4.6 | 14 | Lighter and desaturated (C 0.199→0.141) |
| success on surface-dark | #22c55e | **#41d870** | 4.8 | 5 | Slightly lighter; hue and chroma kept |
| muted on surface-dark | #666666 | **#919191** | 4.7 | 17 | Lighter neutral grey |

The success fix on `surface` and the primary and accent fixes on `surface-dark` needed desaturation. Changing lightness alone topped out at 2.2, 2.2 and 2.8 respectively, and `klar find` exits 1 in that case. I applied `--allow-desaturation` for those three. Trading chroma for contrast is a brand decision, so check that they still look like your brand colors.

Two of the results are close to the threshold: primary on `surface-dark` at exactly 4.5, and accent on `surface-dark` at 4.6. I can re-run any of them with a higher target for more margin.

## Fixes

Each fix keeps the token's hue and changes only lightness, unless the notes column says otherwise. Drift is deltaE. Below 3 is imperceptible, 5–10 is noticeable, 11–20 is clearly different, and above 20 is very different.

| Pair | Proposed fix | New OKCA | Drift (deltaE) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| muted on surface-dark | #666666 → **#919191** | 4.7 | 17 | Lightness only. |
| primary on surface | #3b82f6 → **#115bcc** | 5.0 | 15 | Lightness only. |
| accent on surface | #e94560 → **#bf103f** | 4.7 | 13 | Lightness only. |
| success on surface-dark | #22c55e → **#41d870** | 4.8 | 5 | Lightness only. Cheapest fix, barely noticeable. |
| success on surface | #22c55e → **#047f38** | 4.6 | 22 | Needs chroma reduction (lightness alone tops out at 2.2). Reads as a different, darker green. |
| accent on surface-dark | #e94560 → **#fe8a93** | 4.6 | 14 | Needs chroma reduction (lightness alone tops out at 2.8). Lighter and pinker. |
| primary on surface-dark | #3b82f6 → **#7bacfc** | 4.5 | 13 | Needs chroma reduction (lightness alone tops out at 2.2). Only just clears 4.5. |

## Decisions for you

- **Three fixes cost saturation.** Nudging lightness can't get success on light, or accent and primary on dark, to 4.5, because these saturated colors have a narrow displayable lightness range. I applied `--allow-desaturation` to get those three values, but whether to accept that is a brand call. The success-on-light fix (deltaE 22) is the biggest visible change.
- **One token needs two values.** Each of `primary`, `accent`, `success` and `muted` fails on one or both backgrounds, and no single value fixes both. Light and dark need separate tokens, for example `primary-on-light` #115bcc and `primary-on-dark` #7bacfc. Otherwise pick one background per token.
- **Large text and UI elements need less.** If any of these are only used at 24px or larger, or as icons and borders, the bar is 3.0. Success on dark (3.4) would then pass as it is. Primary and accent on light (2.9 and 2.8) would miss by a hair.
